decisions.context: Which buyer? Separately: what is the ~1,400 'still by hand' firms figure? Is it a count of firms observed spreading by hand, or roughly the NACFB membership size? Settle this by pulling the BridgeTrade notes and asking 3 brokers what they send and whether the lender redoes it.

Brokers: they package and spread to get approvals faster and would pay per deal
Pain sits with lender analysts but the budget sits with a COO or CTO who buys platforms, not memos
Neither pays for a product; the only paid route is a consulting assessment

decisions.context: What they do today, and why it's tolerable: a 10–50 person non-bank lender may already get categorised transactions from an open-banking or accounts vendor (e.g. Codat, Experian, Validis, Ocrolus) or from its loan-origination system, leaving only the memo, which is the analyst's judgement and the part they least want to hand over. Find out with a stack question in each interview.
options: Excel and Word only, no vendor; spreading really is manual
A categorisation or open-banking vendor already does the spreading; only the memo write-up is manual
The loan-origination or credit platform has spreading built in
Spreading is outsourced or offshored cheaply

decisions.context: Who actually demands traceability? 'Compliance asks where a figure came from' assumes a regulator, funder or auditor who checks. Much limited-company SME lending is outside FCA regulation, so the pressure may come from warehouse funders, British Business Bank guarantee-scheme audits, or credit committees. That is a different buyer and a different pitch. Ask each head of credit for their last audit or funder finding on credit files.
options: Warehouse or debt funders audit credit files and have raised findings
Government guarantee-scheme audits (e.g. British Business Bank) check file evidence
Internal credit committee or risk only; no outside pressure
Nobody asks; traceability is a nice-to-have
Don't know

decisions.context: Why now, and does it survive a reversal? The differentiator answers LLM-invented figures, but that only matters to lenders who are using LLMs on memos. If they aren't, the problem isn't theirs yet. If incumbents ship cited memos (Plaid has just launched LendScore 2), the edge goes. Answer with a source search plus one interview question: 'Have you tried an AI tool on memos, and what went wrong?'
options: Contacts are trialling LLM memo tools and have caught invented figures first-hand
They aren't using LLMs and don't plan to soon (the hallucination argument doesn't land)
An incumbent vendor already offers or has announced cited memo generation in the UK
Owner's inference only; no buyer or public source yet
